messages:
sam: Hey team — SparrowHealth signed an LOI and wants a Private POC (VPC + BYOK). Timeline = ~2 weeks. Can we list exact artifacts we need from them and any internal blockers?
priya: Nice! Quick clarifying Qs: do they want our Private control plane inside their VPC (private endpoints) or a customer-managed control plane (air-gapped)? Also, which HSM/KMS provider are they using?
sam: They want Redwood Private (customer VPC peering / Private EPs), not fully air-gapped. They have AWS CloudHSM + a KMS CMK in their account. They said they'll create a cross-account role for us and want ephemeral client certs for mTLS.
oliver: Ok — infra checklist (short):
- CMK ARN + AWS account id (we need to verify key policy)
- Cross-account IAM role ARN that allows sts:AssumeRole from our service principal
- If CloudHSM: HSM cluster id, subnet placement, and schedule for attestation (we need vendor attestation before production use)
- VPC peering/tgw or PrivateLink endpoint details + list of subnets and SGs to allow 443 and the control plane ports
- CIDR ranges for routing, and an admin bastion host public key if they want us to run bootstrap work
priya: For the BYOK/KMS bits, ask them to attach this minimal policy (example) to the CMK or add as a grant so we can GenerateDataKey and Decrypt: 
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodPoc",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-poc-access"},
      "Action": ["kms:GenerateDataKey*", "kms:Decrypt", "kms:Encrypt"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```
(They can restrict Resource to the CMK ARN.)
priya: For certificate handshake we support two flows:
1) CSR flow — customer generates key + CSR and we sign with our intermediate CA (we share cert chain)
2) ACM PCA — customer issues us a subordinate CA and we mint ephemeral certs via API (preferred for automation)
sam: They prefer CSR flow for now. Priya — what do we need from them exactly?
priya: Ask them to generate client private key and CSR. Example: `openssl genrsa -out client.key 2048 && openssl req -new -key client.key -out client.csr -subj "/CN=sparrow-client"` and paste the PEM CSR into the SSO/secure link. We'll sign and return `client.crt` + full chain. Also ask for a contact for cert rotation and the rotation cadence.
lisa: Security checklist items from my side:
- Completed Security Questionnaire (section: key storage, rotation, HSM attestation)
- KMS key policy copy + evidence of CMK in their account
- Network segmentation diagram showing the VPC peering/endpoint and control-plane/VPN flows
- SOC2 / ISO related needs (if they insist on audit reports)
Also: we need assurance they will not disable `kms:DisableKey` for the CMK during the POC.
oliver: Internal blockers: we need an IAM role ARN they created (with trust for `arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/service` — placeholder) and an ETA for HSM attestation (usually 3-5 business days). If attestation slips we can run against a KMS-only flow while waiting.
sam: Pricing / sales note: POC will be covered under PO but we should capture potential additional work (bastion setup, attestation support) as billable. I'll flag in the SOW.
priya: Operational handoff: I'll prepare a short runbook for engineers: minimal terraform snippets for endpoint, sample IAM trust policy, and the CSR submission link.
infra-bot: scheduled: create-poc-staging-environment for sparrowhealth on 2025-06-10T09:00Z (task created #4589)
lisa: I'm happy to review the signed certs and validate the key policy when they send it. Also will consult on rotation TTL (we usually recommend 30 days for ephemerals, 90 for long-lived certs).
sam: Plan: sam -> gather customer artifacts today: CMK ARN, role ARN, CSR (if they already made one), VPC peering details. Priya -> runbook + cert sign flow. Oliver -> prepare staging infra and fallback KMS-only path. Lisa -> security review. Target dry-run on staging next Tue. Thanks :thumbsup:
priya: I'll draft the email to the customer with exact artifacts and paste it here for review before sending.
sam: Perfect — drop updates here.
